p: The **kilowatt hour** is a unit of **energy**: 1 kWh is the energy used when 1 kilowatt of electricity is used for 1 hour. 1 kWh = 3,6 × 10⁶ J.
**Energy in kWh = power in kW × time in h.** Cost = energy in kWh × the price per kWh.
**Never write kW/h.** Never mix Wh and kWh.

screens.q: Which of these is NOT a unit of power?
choices: The watt is the unit of power.
The kWh is a unit of energy: kW × h.
A joule per second is a watt.
screens.why: The kWh is a unit of energy (kW × h). IEB May 2021 P1 Q1.2.

screens.q: A heater is rated 2 500 W. Write its power in kW.

traps: W to kW: divide by 1 000, do not multiply.

screens.q: The heater runs for 45 minutes. Write the time in hours.

traps: That is seconds. For kWh the time must be in hours: ÷ 60.

screens.why: 45 ÷ 60 = 0,75 h. (“Errors were made with conversion from minutes to hours.” IEB Examiners’ Report 2021)

screens.h: Worked example 10.10: the cost of using an oven
screens.q: “The cost of electricity is R2,60 per kWh. A 3 000 W electrical oven is used for 45 minutes.” “Calculate the cost of using the oven for 45 minutes.” (4)

lines.side: P in kW, t in hours

ask.prompt: Work out the cost, in rand.

traps: The power must be in kW: 3 000 W = 3 kW.
The time must be in hours: 45 min = 0,75 h.
Power in kW and time in hours: 3 kW and 0,75 h.
That is the energy in kWh. Multiply by the tariff, R2,60 per kWh.

why: Why change to kW and hours before multiplying?
The tariff is per kWh ✓; working in joules (8,1 MJ) is the long way round ✓.

screens.q: “The cost of electricity is R1,20 per kilowatt hour. Calculate the cost of using the pump continuously for 20 minutes.” The pump is rated 750 W. (IEB 2021 P1 Q7.1.2)

traps: Power in kW (0,75 kW) and time in hours (20/60 h).
The time must be in hours: 20 min = 20/60 h.
The power must be in kW: 750 W = 0,75 kW.

screens.q: A 2 000 W kettle is used; electricity costs R2,60 per kWh. For how many hours can R45 of electricity run it?

traps: The power must be in kW: 2 000 W = 2 kW.
Divide the energy by the power: t = energy ÷ P.
That is the energy bought, in kWh. Now divide by the power, 2 kW.
num.hint: Energy bought = 45 ÷ 2,60 kWh. Then t = energy ÷ P, with P in kW.

screens.why: Energy bought = 45 ÷ 2,60 = 17,31 kWh (keep 17,3077 in the calculator). t = 17,3077 ÷ 2 = 8,65 h.

can: Say what a kWh is: a unit of energy.
Change W to kW and minutes to hours before you multiply.
Work out a cost, and work backwards from money to time.
